title: Taiwan Turns Waste Oyster Shells Into a Heater for Ready-to-Eat Meals
summaryZh: 水試所用回收牡蠣殼研發即食餐加熱包，七分鐘水溫達80度。
summaryHi: ताइवान ने बेकार सीप के खोल से तैयार भोजन गर्म करने वाला हीटर बनाया।
summaryEs: Taiwán crea un calentador para comidas listas usando conchas de ostra recicladas.
summaryJa: 台湾、廃棄カキ殻を再利用した非常食用ヒーターを開発。
summaryKo: 대만, 버려진 굴 껍데기로 즉석식품 발열팩 개발.
summaryEn: Taiwan's Fisheries Research Institute has made a meal heater from recycled oyster shells.
paragraphs: A government research body in Taiwan has found a way to turn a common type of seafood waste into something useful. The Fisheries Research Institute, which operates under the Ministry of Agriculture, has developed a self-heating pack for meals ready-to-eat (MREs) using recycled oyster shells.

MREs are sealed meals designed to be eaten in places without kitchens. They are widely used by the armed forces and in disaster relief, and they have also become popular for outdoor activities such as camping. The institute is now promoting its heater to private firms.

The project tackles a growing waste problem. Taiwan discards roughly 160,000 tonnes of oyster shells each year, and although most are reused in animal feed, fertiliser and cat litter, about 23,000 tonnes are still thrown away.

At a press conference, associate researcher Kao Yi-feng explained the science behind the product. Oyster shells consist mainly of calcium carbonate, which turns into calcium oxide when processed at high temperatures. When calcium oxide comes into contact with water, it reacts rapidly and releases a large amount of heat. In tests, 150 millilitres of water reached 80 to 95 degrees Celsius within seven to eight minutes, warming the food to about 50 degrees.

The institute has signed a licensing deal with one company and a separate agreement with another firm to produce seafood-based MREs. It noted that the heaters currently sold in Taiwan are imported and rely on chemical powder mixtures.
Scientists in Taiwan have found a new use for old oyster shells. They used the shells to make a small heater for ready meals.
Soldiers, rescue workers and campers often eat these meals. The meals come in a bag, and the heater makes the food warm without a fire.
Taiwan throws away about 160,000 tonnes of oyster shells every year. Most of them are used again for animal food, plant food and cat litter. But about 23,000 tonnes are still waste.

The shells are cooked at a very high temperature. Then they change into a new material. When you add water, it gets very hot very fast. With a little water, the water reaches 80 to 95 degrees in about seven minutes, and the food gets warm.
The Fisheries Research Institute made the heater. One company can now make it. Today, the heaters sold in Taiwan come from other countries.
sentZh: 台灣的科學家為舊牡蠣殼找到了新用途。
他們用這些殼做出一種給即食餐用的小型加熱包。
軍人、救援人員和露營的人常吃這種餐點。
餐點裝在袋子裡，加熱包不用火就能讓食物變熱。
台灣每年丟棄約16萬公噸的牡蠣殼。
大部分會再被拿來做動物飼料、肥料和貓砂。
但仍有約2萬3千公噸成為廢棄物。
這些殼會在非常高的溫度下加熱處理。
然後它們會變成一種新的材料。
加水時，它會很快變得非常熱。
只要加一點水，大約七分鐘水溫就會達到80到95度，食物也會變熱。
這款加熱包是由水產試驗所研發的。
現在已有一家公司可以生產它。
目前在台灣販售的加熱包都是從其他國家進口的。

paragraphs: Taiwan's Fisheries Research Institute has developed a heater for meals ready-to-eat (MREs) that is made from recycled oyster shells. The institute, which is part of the Ministry of Agriculture, is now offering the technology to private companies.

MREs are packaged meals that can be eaten anywhere. They are used by the military and in disaster relief, and they are also popular with campers. A heater inside the pack warms the food without fire or electricity.
Every year, Taiwan throws away around 160,000 tonnes of oyster shells. Most are reused as animal feed, fertiliser or cat litter, but about 23,000 tonnes end up as waste.

Kao Yi-feng, a researcher at the institute, explained how it works. Oyster shells are mainly calcium carbonate. When they are heated to a high temperature, they become calcium oxide, which reacts quickly with water and gives off a lot of heat. With 150 millilitres of water, the water reaches 80 to 95 degrees Celsius in seven to eight minutes.
One company has already signed an agreement to use the technology. The institute says the MRE heaters now sold in Taiwan are imported and use chemical powders.

隸屬農業部的水產試驗所，現在正把這項技術提供給民間企業。
即食餐是可以在任何地方食用的包裝餐點。
軍隊和救災時都會使用，也很受露營者歡迎。
包裝裡的加熱包不需要火或電就能把食物加熱。
台灣每年丟棄大約16萬公噸的牡蠣殼。
大部分被再利用為動物飼料、肥料或貓砂，但約有2萬3千公噸最後成為廢棄物。
該所研究員高翊峰說明了它的原理。
牡蠣殼的主要成分是碳酸鈣。
加熱到高溫後，它們會變成氧化鈣，而氧化鈣與水快速反應並釋放大量熱能。
加入150毫升的水，七到八分鐘內水溫就能達到攝氏80到95度。
已有一家公司簽約使用這項技術。
水試所表示，目前在台灣販售的即食餐加熱包都是進口的，而且使用化學粉末。

paragraphs: Taiwanese researchers have come up with an inventive answer to a stubborn waste problem. The Fisheries Research Institute, an agency of the Ministry of Agriculture, has created a self-activating heater for meals ready-to-eat (MREs) built from recycled oyster shells, and is now pitching the technology to private industry.

Such meals are a staple for soldiers and disaster relief teams, who often operate far from any kitchen, and they have found a growing market among campers and other outdoor enthusiasts. The heater allows food to be warmed without a flame or a power supply.

The scale of the problem is considerable. Taiwan discards around 160,000 tonnes of oyster shells annually. While the bulk is recycled into animal feed, fertiliser and cat litter, some 23,000 tonnes a year are simply dumped.

Associate researcher Kao Yi-feng outlined the chemistry at a press briefing. The shells are composed largely of calcium carbonate, which is converted into calcium oxide through high-temperature processing. On contact with water, calcium oxide reacts vigorously and gives off substantial heat. Adding 150 millilitres of water raises its temperature to between 80 and 95 degrees Celsius in seven to eight minutes, bringing the meal itself up to around 50 degrees.

Commercial interest is already emerging. The institute has licensed the technology to one company and reached a non-exclusive deal with another to manufacture seafood-based MREs. It also stressed that the heaters now on the Taiwanese market are all imported and depend on blends of chemical powders.
sentZh: 台灣研究人員為一個棘手的廢棄物問題想出了富有創意的解答。
農業部所屬的水產試驗所，用回收牡蠣殼製成一種可自動啟動的即食餐加熱包，目前正向民間產業推銷這項技術。
這類餐點是軍人和救災隊伍的必需品，他們常在遠離廚房的地方作業，而且在露營者和其他戶外愛好者之間的市場也越來越大。
這種加熱包讓食物不需要火焰或電源就能加熱。
這個問題的規模相當可觀。
台灣每年丟棄約16萬公噸的牡蠣殼。
雖然大部分被回收做成動物飼料、肥料和貓砂，每年仍有約2萬3千公噸直接被傾倒。
副研究員高翊峰在記者說明會上概述了其中的化學原理。
這些殼主要由碳酸鈣構成，經高溫處理後轉化為氧化鈣。
氧化鈣一接觸水就會劇烈反應，並釋放大量熱能。
加入150毫升的水，能在七到八分鐘內把水溫提高到攝氏80到95度，讓餐點本身升溫到約50度。
商業上的興趣已經開始出現。
水試所已把這項技術授權給一家公司，並與另一家公司達成非專屬協議，生產以海鮮為主的即食餐。
它也強調，目前台灣市面上的加熱包全都是進口的，而且依賴化學粉末混合物。

paragraphs: A state research agency in Taiwan has demonstrated how agricultural by-products can be given a second life. The Fisheries Research Institute, which falls under the Ministry of Agriculture, has engineered a self-activating heater for meals ready-to-eat (MREs) derived from recycled oyster shells, and is actively seeking partners in the private sector.

MREs are indispensable in military operations and disaster relief, where conventional cooking facilities are rarely available, and they are increasingly popular among recreational campers. A heating element enables the contents to be warmed without either a naked flame or an electricity supply.

The initiative addresses a significant environmental burden. Taiwan generates approximately 160,000 tonnes of discarded oyster shells each year. Although the majority are repurposed as animal feed, fertiliser and cat litter, roughly 23,000 tonnes are disposed of as waste annually.

At a press conference, associate researcher Kao Yi-feng elaborated on the underlying chemistry. Oyster shells consist predominantly of calcium carbonate, which is transformed into calcium oxide when subjected to high temperatures. Upon contact with water, calcium oxide undergoes a rapid reaction that releases considerable heat. With 150 millilitres of water, the pack reaches 80 to 95 degrees Celsius within seven to eight minutes, sufficient to warm the meal to approximately 50 degrees.

The institute has already concluded a licensing agreement with one firm and a non-exclusive arrangement with another to produce seafood-based MREs. It emphasised that existing heaters on the domestic market are entirely imported and rely on chemical powder formulations, implying that a locally sourced alternative could reduce this dependence.
sentZh: 台灣一個國家研究機構示範了如何讓農業副產品重獲新生。
隸屬農業部的水產試驗所，研發出一種以回收牡蠣殼製成的可自動啟動即食餐加熱包，並正積極尋找民間合作夥伴。
即食餐在軍事行動和救災中不可或缺，因為這些場合很少有一般的烹調設備，而且它們在休閒露營者之間也越來越受歡迎。
加熱元件讓餐點內容不需明火或電力就能加熱。
這項計畫處理一個重大的環境負擔。
台灣每年產生約16萬公噸的廢棄牡蠣殼。
雖然大部分被轉作動物飼料、肥料和貓砂，每年仍有大約2萬3千公噸被當作廢棄物處理。
在記者會上，副研究員高翊峰詳細說明了其中的化學原理。
牡蠣殼主要由碳酸鈣構成，經高溫處理後會轉變為氧化鈣。
氧化鈣一接觸水便會發生快速反應，釋放出可觀的熱能。
加入150毫升的水，加熱包在七到八分鐘內就能達到攝氏80到95度，足以把餐點加熱到約50度。
水試所已與一家公司簽訂授權協議，並與另一家公司達成非專屬安排，生產以海鮮為主的即食餐。
它強調，國內市場現有的加熱包全部仰賴進口，而且依賴化學粉末配方，意味著在地取材的替代品可以減少這種依賴。
